supports: AquaCrop scenarios optimized irrigation across a complete wheat–maize rotation under a total-water constraint.
Continuous multi-year simulation captures carry-over soil water and yield-risk consequences that single-season optimization can miss.
limitations: Authors state that calibration/validation was not the focus and mainly default parameters were used. Nutrient stress and genotype differences were omitted. DOI includes 2025 but journal publication year is 2026. Data on request.

sources.evidence_level: publisher results, validation and attribution excerpts
supports: A coupled CWatM–MODFLOW analysis attributes NCP groundwater recovery to water diversions, sectoral demand reductions and climatic conditions.
Recovery attribution depends on the time window; policy initiators and wet-period amplification differ.

sources.evidence_level: publisher abstract and results indexed excerpts
supports: In-situ monitoring documents a reversal of groundwater declines across the plain portion of the Hai River basin after 2020.
Surface-water transfers, groundwater regulation and wet conditions contributed to recent recovery.
limitations: This hydrogeological study’s NCP is approximately 130,000 km² and is not automatically the same as the broader agricultural Huang–Huai–Hai Plain. Later monitoring is denser; original aquifer types and well availability matter.

journal_eligibility.basis: Nature/Science journal family

sources.evidence_level: publisher DOI metadata and co-author institutional deposit
supports: Improving irrigation efficiency alone is insufficient to establish basin-scale water savings; accounting and enforceable water-use controls are needed.
limitations: Policy Forum, not a primary irrigation treatment experiment; use for policy framing and accounting, not site-level numerical response.

critical_scope_notes: The agronomic NCP/Huang–Huai–Hai boundary and the plain portion of the Hai River basin used by groundwater-recovery papers differ; match maps and areas before comparing results.
Irrigation application, groundwater abstraction, ET, root-zone drainage, aquifer recharge and groundwater storage change require separate accounting.
Calibration, assimilated-state agreement and independent treatment validation require distinct labels.
Published management percentages are not results of the present model.
Many relevant treatment papers have data on request; no complete new independent calibration/validation dataset was obtained in this reference task.
